recommendations.text: It is recommended that the measures already initiated by the European Commission against France for not having transposed the requirements of the last modification (Directive 95/29/EC) of Directive 91/628/EEC (see point 5.8.2) be pursued. Certain non-compliances in the application of Directive 91/628/EEC should be included in such a procedure.
France has to take action to ensure compliance with all parts of Directive 91/628/EEC throughout the whole country until 31.12.1998.

The competent Polish authorities at places of departure should ensure that route plans for horses travelling by road and rail from the interior of Poland towards the South of France, foresee unloading and a 24-hour rest period on their long way. The competent German or French authorities on the way should enforce this (e.g. at Lauterbourg, France, actually a transfer point, that should then be upgraded to a staging point).

The competent German, Dutch and French authorities at places of departure should ensure that route plans for cattle travelling by road and sea to North African countries, foresee unloading and a 24-hour rest period at the transfer points (French Mediterranean ports). The competent French authorities at the ports should enforce this.

It is recommended to invite representatives of Member States to the services of the Commission to discuss how progress could be achieved to improve cooperation between Member States in the field of long-distance transports of animals, in particular with regard to the length of transport aboard ferry boats, to the requirements for loading densities during combined road-and-ferry journeys and to the necessity to exclude animals in advanced pregnancy from being transported.

It is recommended to modify EC legislation in the following areas: · new forms for route plans should be elaborated, · a more precise definition for animals in advanced pregnancy (see point 5.6) should be formulated.

Recommendations for the Commission services : Having verified that the veterinary authorities have acted in a satisfactory way by improving the four establishments to the required standard, and that action is taken to suspend the approval of the fifth establishment, consideration should be given to suspending the infringement proceedings opened by Commission (reference A/96/2022) against France while waiting for further guarantees from the French authorities.

Recommendations for the French authorities : Further information on the follow-up of the fifth establishment and its supervision should be provided by the French Authority by August 1999 and eventually verified on the spot. 7

Recommendations to the Commission services ·Consideration should be given to legal proceedings being taken against the France on the grounds that the veterinary presence as required by Council Directive 71/118/EEC is not guaranteed in all slaughterhouses and cutting plants. ·Consideration should be given to legal proceedings being taken against France on the grounds that the ante and post-mortem inspection as required by Council Directive 71/118/EEC is not guaranteed in all slaughterhouses and farms. · The Commission should determine the general criteria for the special training for the staff of the undertaking in order to carry out operations provided in (a) and (b) of the second paragraph of point 47 of Chapter VIII of Annex 1, Council Directive 71/118/EEC, under the direct supervision of the official veterinarian, a foreseen in art. 8. thirth paragraph. · Legal opinion should be provided on the interpretation given by the French authorities that "transport between establishments of the same group is not considered as putting on the market and this type of transport should not be covered by the required documentation".

Recommendations to the Member State · The CCA of France should remedy without delay the deficiencies referred to in the conclusions. The rectification of the deficiencies in regard to the veterinary supervision of the establishments (paragraph 3.6), the ante mortem (paragraph 3.5), post-mortem (paragraph 3.7) and slaughter hygiene (paragraph 3.8) is of special importance as those are the basic elements to guarantee the hygienic quality in fresh poultry meat production. · The CCA of France should inform the Commission within two months of receipt of the final report of the actions either taken or planned to remedy the deficiencies identified and should indicate a clear timetable for all actions specified. 26

Consideration should be given to using the Buffered rose bengal agglutination test (USDA card test) by the State Veterinarian in charge of herds which have demonstrated a reactor to other tests. This will have the effect of rapidly identifying additional within herd- infected animals and lead to their quick removal thus avoiding subsequent within herd spread and therefore reducing the risk of spread to contiguous herds. It is cheap to perform, can be carried out on the farm and it is efficient at identifying early infection.
Consideration should be given to automating the reading of the results of the RBT, thus reducing within laboratory error.

The French authorities should apply current EU legislation concerning testing prior to movement (SAT). With a view to using alternative methods, they should immediately apply to the Commission for the provision of footnote 6 of Annex F, model 1, under the procedure as outlined in Article 17 (Standing Veterinary Committee) of Council Directive 64/432/EEC, on health problems affecting intra- Community trade in bovine animals and swine, as last amended by Council Directive 98/99/EC, to be applied. This will have the effect of legitatimising the CFT for trade. 9.2. To the Commission services: 9.2.1. The Commission services should organise an inspection mission to evaluate progress in two years time. 18

Provide a response, within one month of receipt of the translated final report, giving details of the actions, taken and planned to address the deficiencies relating to the facilities (construction only) referred to in this report; along with a timetable for completion of these actions. All deficiencies should be corrected within 6 months of receipt of the translated final report.

Provide a response, giving within one month of receipt of the translated final report, details of the actions, taken and planned to address the other deficiencies referred to in this report (hygiene, procedure, equipment, veterinary staff, documentation, registration and fees) along with a timetable for completion of these actions. In any event all deficiencies should be corrected within 3 months of receipt of the translated final report. 7.2. To the Commission It is recommended that the Commission: 7.2.1. Consider a meeting with Swiss authorities to discuss the lack of necessary facilities for live animals and products in Saint-Louis-Bâle in relation to the below mentioned recommendation 1/94. 7.2.2. Consider reviewing recommendation 1/94 of the agreement of the joint Commission of CEE-Switzerland in the light of the fact there are no necessary facilities available for live animals for Saint-Louis-Bâle (road and rail) on Swiss territory.

Consider withdrawal of the approval for the border inspection posts mentioned in relation to the different categories if satisfactory guarantees are not provided within the regarded time limit or if the time limits submitted by the French Authorities are not met: - Saint-Louis-Bâle (rail): products (NHC) - Saint-Louis-Bâle (road): products (NHC and HC) - Saint-Louis-Bâle (airport): live animals (O) 18 - Le Havre: products (HC-NT and NHC-NT) - Orly: products (NHC and HC-NT)
Consider amending the Annex to Commission Decision 92/527/EEC so that information on action taken regarding rejected consignments of live animals can be included.

Consider taking action in response to the French Authorities' failure to transpose Directive 97/78/EC into French legislation. 19 8. To take urgent corrective action in regard to the establishment visited, where a significant public health risk was identified.

To ensure correct implementation of the EU provisions in regard to the approval of the establishments, issuing export certificates, the use of ionisation in meat preparation, the use of mechanically recovered meat and the exemption of the EU approval for certain meat products establishments.
To rectify deficiencies encountered in the plants visited and to ensure that any similar deficiencies receive attention in all other plants in France.

To inform the remaining competent authorities at the Département level of the outcome of the mission in order that they can take all the necessary measures to ensure compliance of the establishments with the EU requirements.

To strengthen veterinary supervision by the competent authority at the Département level in order to monitor satisfactorily both the compliance by the establishments with EU requirements and the performance of supervisory activities in the plants. The veterinary supervision should include corrective mechanisms for deficiencies identified.
To ensure the competent authorities at the Département level have, and make use of, the power to take all the necessary actions vis à vis individual establishments.
To ensure the control by the central competent authority over the competent authorities at the Département level.

To ensure formal communication between the two authorities involved in the supervision in the establishments. The central competent authority was asked to inform the Commission services of the action taken in response to point 7.1.1 within two days of receiving the text of the individual report on the establishment concerned. The CCA responded on 13/4/2000. A plan concerning action to be taken regarding the implementation of recommendations to points 7.1.2 to 7.1.8 should be provided to the Commission within three months of receipt of the final report. This plan should include timetables for the completion of the action required. 20/12/00 - 23843 14 7.2 To the Commission Services 7.2.1. To consider developing Community guidelines for the performance of official controls in the production of meat products and minced meat/meat preparations. ADDENDUM TO THE MISSION RERPORT DG (SANCO)/1066/2000 Competent authority response to the mission report: The French authority responded satisfactorily within the defined deadline to the recommendation at point 7.1.1. of the report. 20/12/00 - 23843 15
In a letter dated 5 July 2000 the French competent authorities provided detailed information on the action planned in the slaughterhouse referred to in point 8.1.1.

A letter dated 14 July 2000 from the FVO to the French authorities requested additional guarantees for certain deficiencies noted during the mission in the establishment where these were felt not to have been fully addressed in their initial response.

In a letter dated 28 July 2000, the French Authorities gave additional guarantees as requested In respect of the draft mission report, the French authorities also provided comments as reflected in this final report, in their letter, dated 28 July 2000 (see point 3 above). Page 17 of 17

To the competent authority of France · To bring certification procedures into compliance with the requirements of Council Directive 96/93/EC. · To ensure that the tests required by Council Directive 64/432/EEC are carried out and, further, to ensure that they are carried out on the premises of origin rather than in assembly centres, as required by the Directive.9 · To complete the transposition of Council Directives 96/93/EC and 97/12/EC. The competent authority should indicate in writing to the Commission, within one month of receipt of the final report, the timetable which it proposes for compliance with these recommendations.

To the Commission Services To consider measures to improve the identification of destination addresses by the Animo system. 9 In view of the legislative changes, described in footnote 6, which have been made since 1th6/e06/00 - 12095 mission was carried out, this recommendation is withdrawn. 9 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/1092/2000 Competent Authority response to the recommendations in the report: The Competent Authority responds by indicating, in respect of the first recommendation, that it disagrees with the mission team's interpretation of Council Directive 96/93/EC and considers that its procedures are already in compliance with the directive. In respect of the third recommendation, it has indicated that the process of transposition is in its final stages. The second recommendation in the draft report has been withdrawn in the light of legislative changes at Council and Commission made subsequent to the mission. 16/06/00 - 12095 10

To provide a response, giving details of the actions taken and planned to ensure that the deficiencies referred to in this report relating to the proposed BIP in Vatry Airport are corrected. 7.2. To the Commission Services It is recommended to the Commission Services: 7.2.1. To consider approval for Vatry airport as a BIP approved for products fit for Human Consumption under Temperature Control (HC-T) for chilled packed products only, if satisfactory written evidence of corrective action undertaken in relation to the deficiencies found is received from the French Authorities. 8 OJ L 331, 17.11.1992 24/05/00 - 11463 9 OJ L 164, 21.06.1997 10 OJ L 59, 28.02.1997 7

To add a new footnote to the annex of Commission Decision 97/778/EC (as amended) for the listing of products under temperature control, "chilled products only". 24/05/00 - 11463 8 8. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/1165/2000 Statements of the Competent Authority to the recommendation 7.1. in this report 8.1 Installation The deficiencies are rectified or going to be rectified (lock on the door of the rejected product store, external canopy of the entrance to the unloading/ unpacking area, hot water supply in laboratory) 8.2 Equipment Equipment is completed (knives and labels for samples). 8.3 Hygiene Hygienic necessities are in place. The drain of the cold store will be corrected to avoid pooling of liquid on the floor. 8.4 Documentation and registration Documentation is completed and classification system restructured. The computerised register will be modified to add the missing data fields. 24/05/00 - 11463 9
The French authorities should envisage measures to ensure that the responsible services can deal more effectively and rapidly with instances of non-compliance with the feed ban.

Although a total feed ban has been in force since 14 November 2000 DGCCRF should continue checking compliance and take samples. On farm mixers and farms should be controlled with a higher frequency than before the total feed ban in order to control the possible illegal use of meat and bone meal. 8.1.2. Epidemio surveillance 1. The competent authority should amend the definition of a BSE suspect in French legislation to bring it into line with the definition in Commission Decision 98/272/EC. 2. The competent authority should consider introducing measures to ensure that the identity and age of the animals sampled in rendering plants and collection points can be more effectively ascertained also in the regions not belonging to the Grand West. 8.1.3. Specified risk material 1. The French competent authorities should ensure that specified risk material is properly stained. 2. The competent authorities should ensure that superficial contamination of the carcasses with spinal cords is prevented at the point of removal.

In order to permit an accurate reconciliation, the competent authorities should ensure that official veterinary inspectors at slaughterhouses receive the acknowledgement sent by the rendering plant in due course.
Council Directive 96/93/EC should be complied with if veterinary certificates are to be used for consignments of meat and bone meal sent from rendering plants for destruction.
The French Authorities should guarantee that the health mark should be applied after the removal of specified risk material.

DGAL should consider measures to guarantee uniform specified risk material controls in the slaughterhouses. 29 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT 1262/2000 Competent Authority response to the recommendations in the report The French authorities stated in their comments that: Ø A new instruction was drafted at the end of 2000 by the DGCCRF. This instruction envisages a plan for taking 2000 samples of raw materials, feed for ruminants and feed for species other than ruminants. Ø Instructions will be issued and sent to the decentralised services in order to amend the definition of a BSE suspect and to bring it into line with the definition in Commission Decision 98/272/EC. Ø Instructions will be issued and sent to the decentralised services to ensure that the identity and age of the animals sampled in rendering plants and collection points can be more effectively ascertained also in the regions not belonging to the Grand West. 30
The competent authority submitted comments on the draft report which were taken into consideration prior to the preparation of the final report.

In these comments the CA made the following comments on several of the above recommendations: Regardi 1 the CA declared that the inspection programme for certain farm animals will be revised. The CA stated that the further establishment of the quality assurance scheme will lead to a more harmonised implementation of the inspections and follow-up. The Procureurs in the départements will be made aware about animal welfare issues in order to ensure a more effective follow-up. 28/03/01 - 46557 25

The major deficiencies related to the procedures should be corrected immediately and in particular: France should ensure that the decision for the introduced consignments of live animals and products other than fishery products is taken by the official veterinarian who signs the Border Crossing Certificates and the Annexes B and not by his technical assistant. All consignments from third countries subject to veterinary checks are under the supervision of the official veterinarians and are checked in accordance with the requirements laid down in Council Directives 97/78/EC, 91/496/EEC and related Commission Decisions.

Action should be taken to correct the other deficiencies noted in this report [general conclusion, veterinary staff, facilities (other than construction), equipment, hygiene, documentation, registration, identification and selection, procedure, transit/warehouse- intracommunity trade procedures, kitchen waste and fees]. In any event all deficiencies should be corrected within three months of receipt of the translated final report and in particular: BIP staff: 40 See footnote 12 32 Shortage of staff in all BIPs, except in Toulouse-Blagnac and in particular shortage of veterinary staff in Marseille port and Marseille airport. Inadequate training of staff for procedures, in particular for Marseille airport. Facilities: The deficiencies related to the facilities for products in Toulouse- Blagnac and for live animals in Marseille port, Marseille airport and Roissy Charles-de-Gaulle should be corrected.

The major deficiencies of the facilities (construction other than those in 8.1.2) referred to in this report should be corrected within six months of receipt of the translated final report and in particular for: Nice, Marseille port, Marseille airport, Saint-Julien-Bardonnex, Sete and Roissy Charles-de-Gaulle for products. Nice, Saint-Julien-Bardonnex and Toulouse-Blagnac for live animals. 8.2. To the Commission It is recommended that the Commission Services: 8.2.1. Consider withdrawal of the approval of the border inspection posts mentioned under 8.1.1., 8.1.2. and 8.1.3. if satisfactory guarantees in relation to the approval (type of category) are not provided within the relevant time limit by the French Authority. 8.2.2. Consider limiting the approval for the BIPs of Toulouse-Blagnac, Saint-Julien-Bardonnex, Nice, to packed products only (footnote 2) if satisfactory guarantees in relation to the approval (type of category) are not provided within the relevant time limit by the French authority. 8.2.3. Consider laying down detailed rules in relation to the approval of the BIP and the related inspection centres.
Consider reviewing the model of the Border Crossing Certificate laid down in Commission Decision 92/527/EEC with regard to point 13 c and footnote 5 in the model.

Consider reviewing the Recommendation n° 1/94 of the EEC/Switzerland Joint Commission in relation to the modification of the approval of Saint-Julien-Bardonnex. 33 9. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/3210/2001 Competent authority response to the recommendations in the report 9.1. Response to recommendations 8.1.1. Under French legislation technical assistants are not allowed to sign Annexes B for other than fish products and an instruction note has been sent to the BIPs, via the Directors of the veterinary services concerned, reminding them of the rules for the supply of staff required and rectify this irregularity. For the BIP of Nice the signing of documents by the technician can be rectified and all identity checks and taking of samples are conducted on the premises of the BIP. For Marseille airport for the checking of manifests the responsible veterinarian was instructed to ensure that a sample check of manifests is organised. The recruitment of a veterinarian should make it possible to rectify the deficiencies in the procedures. 9.2. Response to recommendations 8.1.2. General conclusion: Applications for the approval of border inspection posts in Guadeloupe and Martinique are currently being drawn up in the light of the work currently under way to ensure that these posts operate and are equipped in line with Community requirements. Live animals and animal products or products of animal origin which are imported into these overseas Departments are used and consumed there and are not sent on to France. The error of the Order for Vatry will be rectified. Staff: The central authorities are investigating the possibility of increasing the number of staff in the border inspection posts in Roissy Charles de Gaulle, Sete, Marseille port and airport and Saint Julien Bardonnex. Recruitment of a veterinarian has been requested for Marseille port. A veterinarian was recently assigned to the Marseille airport. A technical and administrative assistant will be recruited in Saint Julien Bardonnex. This September, a new position for a specialised technician was created for the BIPs in Marseille port and airport and Roissy Charles de Gaulle. From September 2001 an additional veterinarian will be in the BIP of Nice. The veterinary assistant has been trained on all veterinary procedures and how to send ANIMO messages in Marseille airport. An individual training plan was offered to some agents in order to rectify the irregularities resulting from a lack of training. Equipment: The French authority informed the Commission that thermometers, pH- meters, saws and refrigerator/freezers had been obtained in accordance with the comments in the tables in point 5.3. 34 For the BIP of Nice a photocopier and a transponder were purchased. For the BIP of Marseille port IC "bassin" west a locker for the changing room, a pH-meter, a refrigerator/freezer, scissors, knives and a stainless steel table were purchased. For the IC "bassin" east a pH-meter, a storage cabinet and a clothes locker, a refrigerator/freezer and a stainless steel table were purchased. The technical equipment for the other animals (inspection and catching equipment, cages for small animals) is foreseen. Full administrative equipment (telephone, fax, photocopier) is foreseen for centres IC2 and IC3. For the BIP of Marseille airport a refrigerator/freezer and a weighing machine were purchased. Technical equipment is planned for the other animals and the NHC-NT products. Cages are planned for the small animals room. For the BIP of Saint Julien Bardonnex a list of missing equipment was drawn up and the equipment concerned was installed. For the BIP of Sete in IC Frontignan a laser thermometer, an answering machine (not requested) and a photocopier were purchased. For the BIP of Roissy Charles de Gaulle three probe thermometers, a transponder, three heat-sealing machines for sample bags, a drill, four sample trays, a bull holder, ropes and halters, a freezer and a refrigerator have been purchased. Three fax machines, a mobile telephone and a photocopier for replacement were purchased. Hygiene: Washing, disinfecting and hand-drying equipment has been installed in all the BIPs visited and in the inspection centres. The managers of the BIPs mentioned under point 5.3. have been reminded to use them according to the provisions relating to hygiene and cleanliness. For the BIP of Nice the veterinarian of the BIP has drawn a programme for regular cleaning and disinfecting of the facilities. Measures were taken for the inspection premises to be devoted solely to inspection. For the BIP of Marseille port "bassin" east cleaning will be carried out by a firm under the supervision of the veterinary services. For IC1 a changing room is to be set up and the room currently used will be used for storing cleaning equipment. For IC2 hot water will be provided in washbasin. For IC3 a locker will be provided and the changing facilities will be restricted to the veterinary services. A wash basin will be installed in the equidae inspection room. Maintenance will be carried out by Marseille port. For the BIP of Marseille airport the inspection room for HC-products has got hot water. A washing and changing room with clothes locker will be kept solely for the use of the veterinary services. The work on the defective frozen store with ice has been entrusted to a maintenance firm. For the BIP of Saint Julien Bardonnex a soap and disinfectant dispenser was installed. For the BIP of Toulouse Blagnac cleaning of the surroundings of the BIP will be conducted regularly by a firm. 35 For the BIP of Sete a reminder was sent to the manager of the site for cleaning and maintenance regularly. For the BIP of Roissy Charles de Gaulle the managers have been reminded for the provisions to hygiene and maintenance of the rooms of the BIP. A plan for cleaning and maintenance has been drawn up by the responsible veterinarian in conjunction with the managers of the facilities, which will be regularly monitored. Documentation: the documentary deficiencies found have now been rectified and the veterinarians at the airport BIPs have been informed about the IATA regulations. Registration: For the BIP of Saint Julien Bardonnex the register for live animals is now available in accordance with the provisions of Commission Decision 97/794/EC. The BIP veterinarians have been reminded for the registration so that the records of imported and redispatched consignments to be completed. Procedures: a reminder has been issued to all BIPs visited of the rules for carrying out the import checks. - Notification of consignments: a memo has been written to operators and importers for the conditions of notifications and the deadlines for pre- notification before the consignments arrive. The competent authority requests the Commission how best to correct the Annexes B and what are the means of authentication and how to follow-up cases of difference of the information between health documents and Annex B. The BIP veterinarians have been instructed to ensure distribution of information for customs destination on Annex B to the operators. - Documentary checks: BIPs have been reminded of the rules for documentary checks and for route plans. - Identity checks: the competent authority in case of split consignments in particular for air transport, when the consignments are smaller than stated in the health certificate, will turn back any consignment if they suspect irregularities in the procedures or the veterinary certification. - Physical checks: the check list will be completed for the temperature of the consignment. Relations between the veterinary authorities and the laboratories are currently being formalised. A system for computer tracking of samples and their results is under development. For route plans it was requested from the BIPs to pay particular attention. - Decision on the consignment: The remarks on the performance of the checks and the documents relating to the results of these checks have been passed on to the veterinarians responsible for the BIPs so that the necessary changes can be made. - ANIMO: The responsible veterinarians of the BIPs have been reminded of the rules regarding the messages to be sent. 36 Transit and transhipment: the responsible veterinarians of the BIPs were instructed for the procedures and the follow up of the consignments in transit and for the written undertaking to repossess the consignments required from all forwarding agents. Kitchen waste: the responsible veterinarians of the BIPs were reminded to record the results of the checks for kitchen waste. A note was sent to all the Directors on 3 April 2001, in order to ensure that all ports and airports which do not have a BIP are covered, stating that all kitchen waste and products intended for consumption by the crew and passengers on board means of transport must be destroyed by incineration when unloaded. 9.3. Response to recommendations 8.1.3. The French authorities set out below the measures already taken or currently being taken as follows: For the BIP of Nice is proposed to limit the approval to packed products (HC-T(1), HC-NT, NHC). The possibilities of restructuring the BIP are studied. Three separate BIPs will be set up in Marseille: BIP Marseille Airport, BIP Marseille Port and BIP Marseille Fos-sur-Mer Port with the corresponding changes to staffing and ANIMO terminal for the BIP Fos-sur-Mer. For the BIP of Marseille Port for "bassin" west a plan to build a new inspection centre for HC and NHC products was being studied. For the BIP of Marseille Airport the rooms used for the storage of HC- products at controlled temperature (chilled, frozen) and a room for storage at ambient temperature will be clearly marked for the use of the BIP. The room used for the checks of all other animals is also used for aquarium fish and is clearly marked. For the BIP of Saint Julien Bardonnex reorganisation of the animal station is planned. This facility is funded jointly by the French and the Swiss authorities and the work will comprise the following: connecting the waste water pipes to the city of Geneva's sewage system, building a loading bay for lorries, internal panels for the crushes for inspecting small ruminants and painting work. For the BIP of Toulouse-Blagnac there will be two separate rooms for other live animals (one for housing the animals and the other for inspection). The limit of the approval to packed products is proposed. For the BIP of Sete a plan for reorganising the premises is under negotiation. The French authorities withdrew the approval of the IC2 of the BIP for the category NHC-products under temperature control. For the BIP of Roissy Charles de Gaulle the inspection centre IC3 was closed with effect from 15 July 2001. For IC5 the NHC-products approval has been withdrawn. For IC1 and IC2 the missing rooms could be established (NHC inspection rooms, rooms for storage at ambient and chilled temperature). 37

audits.title: Fishery products and live bivalve molluscs

recommendations.text: Guarantees received regarding the followi s: Measures already taken 8.1.1. Competent authority - The CA answered that the work to improve the harmonisation of the activities of the decentralised services has already begun. It was decided at a meeting held on 31 January 2002 to establish national inspection procedures as soon as possible. The application of these national inspection procedures will be evaluated in 2002 and 2003. The procedures will pay particular attention to the checking of documentation in establishments and exploitation of the results of own-controls. 8.1.2. Laboratories - Regarding the harmonisation of the methods for the detection of biotoxins, taking into consideration the recommendations of the CRL, the methods have been harmonised since 1 January 2002. The method used for testing for DSP-type diarrhoeic phycotoxins both by the IFREMER laboratories and the laboratories performing analyses for the veterinary services is the modified Yasumoto 1984 method (acetone solvents then dichloromethane), with mice being observed for 24 hours after the start of the test. Henceforth, all the laboratories will therefore participate in the aptitude tests organised by the NRL. 36 Planned Measures 8.1.1. Competent authority - To improve strongly the harmonisation of activities of the inspection services at decentralised level and to improve the supervision of the central level on the decentralised services. The CA informed that a reform of the Veterinary Inspectorate in France is currently being finalised. This reform will create a services inspectorate grade for all the production sectors. It will also create "directeurs régionaux des services vétérinaires" (veterinary services regional directors) whose role will be to ensure harmonisation of inspection practices in all the sectors within their region, and to keep the central administration informed about the implementation of the regulations. Pending the introduction of this reform, assessment and supervision of implementation of the health regulations relating to fishery products, aquaculture products and live bivalve molluscs will be performed by means of audits conducted in the coastal Departments by DGAL representatives (officials of the marine and freshwater products unit) accompanied by representatives of veterinary services of other Departments. The DGAL estimates that it will be able to perform at least six such inspections in 2002, and then twice this number in subsequent years. The CA informed also that an instruction will be issued to the Veterinary Services regarding the approval/suspension of establishments. 8.1.2. Laboratories - To designate a national reference laboratory for monitoring bacteriological and viral contamination of bivalve molluscs and to organise comparative interlaboratory test for enumeration of E. coli in shellfish for all concerned laboratories. The CA informed that the process of designating the national reference laboratory has not yet been completed, but is expected to be so in the course of 2002. - To contact the CRL with regard to the validation of the impedance method used for enumeration of E. coli in shellfish and to fix a programme for validation and the continuous check of the impedance method against the MPN method in all laboratories which use this method. The CRL has been notified of the impedance measurement method used by IFREMER and of the publication of the corresponding AFNOR standard. As soon as the NRL for the microbiological analysis of shellfish has been designated, the recommendations due to be issued by the CRL will be taken into account for the intercomparison tests which the NRL will then organise - To continue the proficiency test for checking the presence of biotoxins in shellfish for all laboratories concerned. All the laboratories, which conduct tests for biotoxins and then analyse any found, will participate in the proficiency tests organised by the NRL from 2002 onwards. 8.1.3. The Competent Authorities should ensure that vertebral columns of bovines aged more than 12 months are systematically removed and disposed of as SRM. 3. The Competent Authorities should ensure that all meat and bone meal and tallow originating from low risk material and produced since 1 April 2001 until the Ministerial Order of 2 October 2001 is fully implemented and effective, is treated as SRM-MBM/tallow and destroyed. 4. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT 3308/2001 Competent Authority response to the recommendations in the report. The French authorities announced in their written comments of 18 February 2002 that they had taken the following actions in relation to the recommendations: BSE epidemio-surveillance. 1. The definition of a BSE suspect will very soon be in line with Regulation (EC) No 999/2001. The Order in question (amendment to the Ministerial Order of 3 December 1990) is being signed. Feed ban. 1. Additional instructions from DGAL are being distributed to the departmental services; it reminds them in particular that specific checks on establishments which distribute and use derogated products must be carried out regularly. 2. Inter-service cooperation is already in hand: most of the general instructions on animal feed are joint or, in the case of individual investigations by one or other of the two authorities (DGAL, DDCCRF), they are drawn up in joint consultation. This cooperation will be formalised in greater detail through the preparation of joint instructions specifying what each service does, for example, in respect of the surveillance and control programmes. The departmental services will also be requested to reinforce their cooperation. 3. Joint instructions are being sent to the DDSVs and DDCCRFs on checks on the transport of processed animal protein. 4. As regards DGCCRF, the annual control programme has been updated for 2002. It has been pointed out in particular that samples must be taken at both the distribution and production stages. 5. Reinforced surveillance of feed for ruminants is included in the programme.
The French authorities will be mindful not to authorise decontamination until the establishment has been approved.

At BIP level the traceability of consignments in accordance with Decision 2001/9 has been improved as the DDSV of the department has set up an information exchange system together with the DDSVs of product destination.
Traceability of consignments leaving approved warehouses has been set in place in accordance with Decision 2001/9/CE.

As regards sampling procedures, in accordance with Directive 76/371/EEC, instructions will be given to the BIPs to set up the necessary sampling system. Specified risk materials (SRM). 1. Steps have been taken to remind the control services (instructions dated 20 November 2001) of the obligations on the industry as regards denaturing SRM. In addition, the risks of superficial contamination of carcasses by spinal 31 cords on their removal have also been identified by the health authorities. This gave rise to an amendment to the Order of 17 March 1992 concerning the requirements to be met by slaughterhouses for the production and placing on the market of fresh meat and laying down the conditions for the health inspection of such establishments (amendment introduced by the Order of 19 July 2001); it requires removal of the spinal cord of bovines aged 12 months and over prior to cutting the carcass into halves by splitting the vertebral column. This requirement, which entered into force on 1 January 2002 in all bovine slaughterhouses, now precludes, on the one hand, the risk of nervous tissue spreading onto the carcass after splitting and, on the other, contamination of the muscle masses next to the vertebral column when the cord is removed manually both by the operators and by the equipment used. 2. As far as the rules are concerned, the requirement to incinerate the vertebral columns of bovines aged 12 months and over was introduced by the Order of 2 October 2001. The formal classification as SRM was officialised by the Order of 4 January 2002. (These two Orders are amendments to the Order of 17 March 1992.) 3. The French authorities ensure that all "low-risk" meal and fats are incinerated. Although, pending establishment of specific collection in the so-called "high- risk" channel of vertebral columns of bovines aged 12 months and over, notably collection from butchers, these products were treated with "low-risk" waste, the Community requirement, that is the incineration of vertebral columns, will be complied with. The French authorities authorise only two types of disposal for the meal produced, direct incineration or storage pending incineration. No processing, including into so-called technical products, is permitted. Furthermore bearing in mind the special requirement in France for a specific dedicated procedure for the production of processed animal protein intended for petfood (as meal from ruminants is prohibited to ensure that there is no cross- contamination resulting from the existence of several channels) and the ban on the use of meal from ruminants in fertiliser production, the only type of disposal for all meal (high and low risk) is incineration. 4. Retaining two channels, high and low risk, could be unwarranted in so far as all products are disposed of by incineration. However, given the limited incineration capacity, the French authorities wanted to retain this separation to ensure priority for just-in-time incineration of TSE risk products and to store only the others. For the special case of the vertebral column, inclusion in the high-risk sector without preparation, notably as regards setting in place new logistics and the selective sorting of bones in the cutting plant, might have resulted in a requirement to store meal also containing dead animals and all SRM. It therefore appeared preferable to store meal containing only bovine vertebral columns, rather than meal containing all SRM, naturally requiring in all cases ultimate incineration 32

The CCA should ensure that a system is developed for the control of route plans so that they are approved only after they have been correctly completed and are returned after the journey (Article 5(d)(ii) of Council Directive 91/628/EEC as amended).

The CA should suspend the approval of the staging point visited until it can meet all the requirements of Council Regulation (EC) no. 1255/97, in particular regarding cleaning and disinfecting as laid down in part A of Annex I.
The CCA should also ensure that all French staging points are operating in compliance with Council Regulation (EC) no. 1255/97.

Ensure that all SRM is properly stained, as already requested in the previous report, and that superficial contamination of small ruminant carcasses with spinal cord is prevented at the point of removal. 2. Instruct the official services responsible for the hygiene controls in down stream establishments to control the complete removal of spinal cord from small ruminants over 12 months of age. 3. Review the current controls of the SRM chain with a view to establishing more harmonised and comprehensive controls of the whole SRM chain including proper record requirements. 22 ADDENDUM TO THE FINAL REPORT Competent Authorities response to the recommendations in the report The French Authorities announced in their written comments of 12 February 2003 that they have taken or will take the following actions in relation to the recommendations: As regards 8.1.1: BSE epidemio-surveillance 1. Instructions are being drafted so that second-level spot checks can be carried out at the abattoir on slaughtered animals, including the category of animals which currently do not undergo the test in order to establish whether they really are not eligible for testing. The French authorities undertake to ask the veterinary authorities concerned to use the records on rendered animals to regularly check whether the number of dead bovines arriving for rendering corresponds to the number of BSE tests carried out in the same rendering plant. 2. The definition of the cohort referred to in the Annex to Regulation (EC) 999/2001 has been applied in full since the publication on 10 December 2002 of the decree of 29 November 2002, which provides for the selective slaughter of animal cohorts in herds in which there has been a confirmed case of BSE. As regards 8.1.2: TSE monitoring in small ruminants 1. The French authorities have taken note of the fact that the FVO wants France to continue to sample a high number of fallen stock in 2003. 2. The French authorities will shortly review the application of the Scrapie monitoring programme for 2002 so that, for 2003, the requirements can be established in light of what has been observed. Over-representation of any group of animals will be avoided where possible. 3. The French authorities will consider whether to review the national rules applicable to the payment of compensation to owners of animals impounded at the abattoir after the CRL has confirmed that they have tested positive. As regards 8.1.3: Feed Ban 1. The French authorities will put in place a more targeted monitoring system for 2003 which takes account of the targeting criteria set out in the Commissio s, which were adopted by the Standing Committee on 20 December 2001. As regards 8.1.4: Specified Risk Materials 1. Together with the federations of the slaughter industry, the French authorities drew up guidelines for the removal of SRM in abattoirs. In view of the recent changes in the legislation and the measures currently under discussion at Community level (tonsils, tongue and head of bovines), these guidelines are now being updated. The work is to be finalised during the present quarter. This work, in which the federations of abattoirs will again be closely involved, will lay down more precise provisions for the denaturing of SRM. The guidelines will also refer to the methods for removing all SRM in order to prevent any contamination of the carcass during these procedures. 23 2. Instructions are currently being drawn up concerning the methods for removing the spinal cord from small ruminants over 12 months of age. These instructions outline the conditions under which the spinal cord should be removed without first splitting the carcass open. They also describe the second-level hygiene checks to be introduced in establishments downstream of the abattoir in order to verify whether the spinal cord has been completely removed at the abattoir. 3. The French authorities will draw up guidelines for inspecting establishments which process by-products and for checking the accounts as regards by-products throughout the SRM chain. The French authorities plan to issue a memorandum for the veterinary authorities in 2003 which will include guidelines for the inspection of processing plants as well as guidelines for checking accounts -- as regards raw or processed by-products. These guidelines should make it possible for reliable checks to be carried out on the movement of products from the point at which they are collected from agri-food establishments until they are ultimately disposed of, as well as their passage through intermediate storage facilities and processing plants. As regards the weighing of SRM, the French authorities have drawn up instructions, which have not yet been approved, for the monitoring authorities. These instructions stipulate that the abattoir should be responsible for weighing high-risk material whenever it is removed, irrespective of whether or not the material is weighed inside or outside the abattoir. A regulation obliging abattoir operators to weigh high-risk by-products, including by- products (such as SRM) removed by public-sector rendering plants, could be adopted during 2003. _____________________ 24

audits.title: Assessment of Mycotoxin, pesticide residues and 3-MCPD contamination and monitoring of irradiated foodstuffs - Import of certain products regarding mycotoxin contamination

recommendations.text: Ensure that non-compliant products are notified rapidly to the Commission RASFF system as required by Article 50 of Regulation 178/2002.
Take steps to ensure that analysis is able to be undertaken rapidly, and to ensure compliance with the 10 day requirement for products to be held.

Take measures to ensure that import controls on foodstuffs of plant origin are reviewed and strengthened, particularly where non-compliance is 26 expected in order to attain a level of official controls at the appropriate stage which will prevent risks to public health within the meaning of Council Directive 89/397/EEC. Given the considerable information existing on recurrent contamination findings the controls should cover a broader variety of products of plant origin.

Enhance import controls on foodstuffs potentially exposed to ionising irradiation. Written assurances should be forwarded to the European Commission with regard to the above recommendations within two months of receipt of the final mission report. The Competent Authority should provide detailed information on the actions that will be taken and propose deadlines by which these actions will be completed. 8.2. To the European Commission Services It is recommended that the Commission services should consider the following actions in respect of the identified conclusions. 1.Amend the reporting format for the co-ordinated Pesticide Monitoring Programme to enable identification of imported products from products from other member states. 9. In future ensure that any information relating to the existence of a serious direct or indirect risk to human health deriving from food in France or other Member States is immediately notified to the Commission via RASFF as per Article 50 of Commission Regulation (EC) No 178/2002.10 10 In their response to the draft report the French Authorities noted that this Regulation entered into force in February 2002. 19

Take urgent steps to ensure all départements are aware of the legal requirement of food business operators to implement autocontrol systems based on the HACCP principals Article 3 of Council Directive 93/43/EEC. 10. ADDENDUM Competent authority response to the recommendations in the report. The French Authorities comment on the first recommendation by stating that the incident took place in 2000 prior to the date of entry into force of Commission Regulation (EC) No 178/2002. In detailed comments on the seco the French authorities noted that an information note from Office C2 of the DGCCRF was distributed to all Départmental Directorates on 1 March 1999 (a copy was attached). The note set out the rules relating to the hygiene of plant products and products of plant origin following transposition of Directive 93/43/EEC on the hygiene of foodstuffs. The French Authorities highlight that this document draws attention, in particular (point 4.3.2.), to the fact that "business operators must implement a HACCP-type system to highlight the specific risks of their activities in order to identify and deal with critical points." The French Authorities stated that these legal requirements will be brought to the attention of Départmental Directorates again in an information note highlighting the risks associated with contaminants. 20

To consider reviewing the approach of supervision carried out by the Competent Authority on the official control activities carried out by the departmental services in order to ensure a uniform approach. With regard to the official inspections in the field of animal nutrition:
To include all stages of the feed chain in drawing up the control programme.
To reflect on the approach used for drawing up the control programme in the light of the risks and the experience gained by both CA in order to make this process more transparent.
To ensure that imported consignments destined for other Member States and suspected of being contaminated with undesirable substances, are not released before the analytical results are available.
To reduce the delays in transmitting the results of the analyses from the laboratory to the CA concerned, and particularly in those cases involving suspicion of contamination.

To draw up a detailed operational contingency plan referred to in Article 4(a) of Directive 95/53/EC, as amended. 24/02/04 - 34964 32 See footnote 26 15 With regard to the approval and registration of establishments and intermediaries operating in the animal feed sector:
To ensure that all mobile-mixers, if relevant, get an approval or registration according to Directive 95/69/EC.

To ensure that all establishments covered by the Directive 95/69/EC fulfill all the necessary requirements laid down in Chapter I of the Annex to that Directive, in particular ensuring the lowest possible level of cross-contamination (Chapter 1.3.(b), paragraph 4 of the Annex to the Directive). 24/02/04 - 34964 16 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT 9059/2003 In their response of 21 January 2004 to the draft report, the French Competent Authority has announced the following actions as initial response to the recommendations made in the report: · The establishment of a regional co-ordinating level for the whole territory of France in 2003, in combination with information provided from a questionnaire to the DDVSs about difficulties in implementing Council Directive 95/69/EC will provide tools for the Central Competent Authority in the harmonisation of the control activities at the departmental level. · In cases involving suspicion of contamination, the DGCCRF laboratories forward the results of analyses as quickly as possible. · A contingency operational plan is being drawn up in the form of a service note that will be distributed to the departmental services. · The DDVS will be requested in course of the year 2004 to draw up lists of mobile mixers. In addition, the professional associations will be requested to provide information too on those operators. ________________________ 24/02/04 - 34964 17

To ensure that there are adequate staff and other resources available at the inspection posts to enable meticulous plant health checks to be carried out on 19 at least a representative sample of all consignments of plants, plant material and other objects listed in Annex VB of Council Directive 2000/29/EC, as required by Article 13(1)(a) of the same Directive.

To ensure that notifications of interceptions are sent to the Commission and other Member States within the timeframe envisaged in Article 2 of Commission Directive 94/3/EC, i.e. `no later than two working days after the date of interception and preferably more rapidly in the case of an interception having involved a refusal'.
To ensure that the SRPV has access to facilities for the proper quarantine of consignments at Marseille, as required by Commission Directive 98/22/EC.

To endorse original phytosanitary certificates and reforwarding certificates, received when the consignment is landed, with an entry stamp from the competent service showing at least the name of the service and the date of entry, in accordance with Article 12 (3) of Council Directive 2000/29/EC. The competent authorities in France are advised:

To consider increasing the amount of publicity available to travellers and the number of controls carried out on passenger baggage at Roissy. France is requested to report to the Commission two months after receipt of the final report, on action taken and/or planned on the recommendations. For planned action, a deadline for completion should be indicated. 20 Addendum The French authorities sent detailed comments regarding the draft report, these are published separately, however in relation to the recommendations, the authorities noted that `the remarks a s made by the FVO report, which were perfectly justified, have been acted on immediately'. The remedial measures taken by the Directorate-General for Food's Subdirectorate for Plant Quality and Plant Protection include centralising the management of staff in the BIPs and reducing the number of BIPs to `match staffing to needs'. In response to recommendations 3, 4 and 5, the authorities made the following comments: `The Marseille BIP has access to storage and refrigeration facilities for intercepted products which we consider to be adequate given the very short storage times. Admittedly, these facilities are not enclosed and reserved exclusively for our own use, but they are satisfactory. The SRPVs keep the country of origin certificates with the carbon copy of the PV04 laissez-passer handed to the Customs. Consequently, validating this certificate by affixing a stamp seems to serve no purpose. Publicity material could be introduced very quickly. Several mock-ups already exist. However, two obstacles stand in our way: the first is budgetary, the second is the reluctance of the airports and airlines to let us communicate with their customers. Controls on passengers will be continued and stepped up once our remedial measures in response to the FVO's recommendations have been implemented.' 21
Rectify the shortfalls relating to the identification of animals, as stated in the recommendations of mission DG(SANCO)/3381/2001.
Continue to update contingency plans for swine fevers.
Complete the update of the contingency plan for FCO (blue tongue).
Ensure that départemental contingency plans are updated throughout national territory.
Supplement contingency plans with specific instructions for use in an emergency in agri-food establishments.

Rectify the shortcomings in the field of general hygiene, operation, animal welfare and post mortem inspection detected in establishments during this mission. 10. Addendum In their response to the draft report of 29 July 2003, reference 692397, the French authorities made a certain number of factual corrections and comments which have been incorporated into the final report. With regard to the recommendations made to the French authorities, the latter have said that they will present their comments on this matter in response to the final report. 3
The CA should take measures to ensure full implementation of Commission Decision 2002/995/EC.

The CA should, within one month of receipt of the translated final report, submit an action plan which provides adequate guarantees that the shortcomings identified in this report in relation to the proposed BIP at Châteauroux-Déols airport are satisfactorily addressed. 8.2. To the Commission Services It is recommended to the Commission Services 1. to consider the approval of the proposed BIP of Châteauroux-Déols airport for HC-T products (products fit for human consumption under temperature control), only packed with the footnote (2), if satisfactory guarantees in relation to the correction of the deficiencies found, are received from the French Competent Authority. 6 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/9159/2003 In response to the recommendations in the draft report, the Central Competent Authority (CCA) in France indicated the followi under point 8.1.1: Decision 2002/995/EC laying down safeguard measures with regard to imports of foodstuffs by travellers has been sent to customs and the airport manager. Wall displays have been installed to inform passengers of these provisions. Checks are now organised by veterinary service staff together with customs staff (3-4 flights per year). Decision 2002/349/EC laying down the list of products subject to veterinary import checks has been sent to customs, the airport manager and the various forwarding agents. The provisions of Decision 2002/995/EC laying down safeguard methods with regard to imports of foodstuffs by travellers are now implemented in full. Recommendation under point 8.1.2: 1. Facilities Approval of the border inspection post has been requested for packed products only. Frozen products will be imported only very rarely, which means that the risk of cross- contamination through product flows is very small, especially as the products in question are of the same nature (products intended for human consumption) and will be packed. Concerning the holding of products in the low-temperature storage area, as stated in the application for approval of the BIP no further batches will be accepted or stored in this area until a consignment already present has been released. However, these arrangements can be reviewed in the light of the actual flows checked by the BIP in practice. 2. Equipment The ANIMO connections have been installed, and a number is in the process of being allocated. The BIP's administrative equipment is thus complete. Seals are now available to the BIP. Its technical equipment is thus complete. 4. Hygiene Disinfecting fluid dispensers have been installed in the inspection room and toilets, thus rectifying the hygiene deficiencies noted. 5. Documentation All the missing documentation has now been provided (EEA Agreement, list of approved BIPs, health certificates for fresh meat). The sample request has been completed by adding the reference to the common veterinary entry document. 6. Notification of consignments In accordance with the provisions of Decision 93/13/EC, the arrival of consignments will be reported using part 1 of the common veterinary entry document, a model of which is attached to the said Decision as Annex B. 7. Kitchen waste Kitchen waste dumped within the airport boundaries will be directly disposed of either by incineration at an approved incineration plant or by depositing it at a landfill site 7 approved under Directive 1999/31/EC, in accordance with the provisions of Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002/EC. 8. Overall assessment The Châteauroux-Déols border inspection post now fully complies with the approval conditions laid down in Decision 2001/812/EC. 8

audits.title: Official foodstuffs control system, implementation of controls on hygiene of foodstuffs, follow up on recommendations of report 3225/2001

recommendations.text: Notify to the Commission the list of approved official control laboratories as required by Article 15 of Council Directive 89/397/EEC.
Ensure that the depth of inspection based on GHP guides is adequate to ensure assessment of the requirements of Article 3(2) of Council Directive 93/43/EEC.
Formalise the involvement of laboratory staff in regional and inter-regional planning meetings.

audits.title: CSF - Classical Swine Fever in wild boars

recommendations.text: To establish a control system to be applied by the CA, containing a programme of inspections on the spot with written instructions on the procedures to be followed, ensuring that the full range of measures of the eradication plan are implemented, in particular concerning animal identification, farm registers, movement of pigs, cleaning and disinfection, registers, collection/transport/storage of samples or animals for CSF diagnosis, and rendering/disposal of animals.
To transpose Council Directive 2000/15, amending Directive 64/432/EEC on health problems affecting intra-Community trade in bovine animals and swine.

To ensure that the requirements of the NPCD are fully in compliance with Article 14 of Council Directive 64/432/EEC, as amended by Directive 2000/15/EC, as well as with Commission Decision 2000/678/EC.

To consider methods for the estimation of the feral pig population and feral pigs found dead or shot during hunting, with the aim of increasing the level of confidence in the intensity of the CSF sampling.
To send the up-dated version of the CP for classical swine fever to the DDSV and to ensure its full implementation at departmental level.

To ensure that the type of samples collected for CSF diagnosis is in accordance with Commission Decision 2002/106/EC, allowing for a range of serological and virological tests, as described in the above Decision, to be performed systematically with the aim of increasing the probability of detecting a case of CSF.

To ensure that delay in CSF diagnosis is shortened, in order to ensure that meat from feral pigs shot in a "potentially infected zone" can only be released for consumption or trade in compliance with the requirements of Article 15(2) (c) of Council Directive 2001/89/EC. The French competent authorities should submit an action plan indicating in detail the action proposed or already taken, within one month of receiving the final translated report. This plan should include deadlines by which the proposed action will be completed. 18 9. ADDENDUM Competent authority response to the draft mission report In reply to the draft mission report the French authorities provided detailed comments in a letter dated 21/09/2004. Where appropriate, their comments have been introduced in the final report, either in the text to correct factual errors or as footnotes. They also provided initial details of their response to certain recommendations made in the report as follows: · Recommendation 8.1 "A programme of inspecting storage centres will be put in place in the Departmental Directorates of Veterinary services (DDSVs) concerned as from 2004/2005 hunting season. The procedures will be prepared in parallel with the implementation of the vaccination campaign. They should be completed drafted and applied by end 2005. As regards identification checks, by 1 January the French authorities will implement controls in pig farms, in the framework of the conditions governing aid". · Recommendation 8.2 "Directive 2000/15/EC is being transposed. However, the adoption of a text of this kind- a Council of State Decree- involves administrative constraints as regards its publication in the French Official Journal, which may take up to six months." · Recommendation 8.3 "Work on the database designed to integrate all the requirements of article 14 of Directive 64/432/EEC will begin once Directive 2000/15/EEC has been transposed." · Recommendation 8.4 "We will continue to reflect on this matter in order to improve the reliability of the data." · Recommendation 8.5 "The version will be sent to the DDVSs in the course of 2005 after supplements have been added." · Recommendation 8.6 "Spleen is the most appropriate sample for investigating the viral genome in the framework or surveillance of the disease and its use is in compliance with Decision 2002/106/EC. We will once again brief the hunters as to the need to take tonsil samples when the spleen has deteriorated." · Recommendation 8.7 "Supplementary resources in terms of laboratory capacity have been made available to ensure compliance with the time limits, notably as regards virological analyses. This includes on the one hand the use of `approved-for-consumption' analyses (analyses libératoires) and, on the other hand, real time surveillance of epidemiological trends." 19

audits.title: Artificial Insemination/Embryo and Semen collection centres

recommendations.text: To transpose completely Council Directive 88/407/EEC, in particular in respect of definition, approval and supervision of SSCs, and Council Directive 89/556/EEC.

To amend the instruction for TB test procedures in order to completely and correctly comply with Point 2.2 of Annex B of Council Directive 64/432/EEC and to implement and to enforce the relevant provisions. 16 http://www.icar.org 18
To keep updated and accurate registers of all approved SCC and approved SSC centres and prevent non-approved SCCs from using an approval number of an approved SCC.
To ensure that the approved SCCs and the approved SSCs are placed under the effective permanent supervision of a CV authorised by the CA (Chapter I of Annex A of Council Directive 88/407/EEC).
To ensure that the official supervision of the SCCs and SSCs is carried out in compliance with Chapter II of Annex A of Council Directive 88/407/EEC.

To ensure that SSCs or storage units of SCCs are supervised in such a way that a record is kept of all movement of semen and of the status of the bulls whose semen is stored there, and which must comply with the requirements of Council Directive 88/407/EEC.

To ensure that quarantine accommodation meets the requirements of Annex B, Chapter I, Point 1. (a) of Council Directive 88/407/EEC, and that direct transfer of bulls is only allowed according to provisions of Annex B, Chapter I, Point 5. thereof.

To ensure that the CA is duly informed of "non-negative" or positive test results of bulls at SCCs in order to take appropriate measures and that the certifying OV does have access to all pieces of information allowing him to draw up certificates in accordance with Council Directive 96/93/EC consistently.

To provide appropriate training for the official supervision of SCCs and SSCs to the OVs responsible. The French competent authorities should submit an action plan indicating the actions taken and planned in response to the recommendations of this report, within one month of receipt of the final translated version of this report. 10.
